title: Dedicated capacity performance gate and load lab
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Establish a repeatable lab and gate for measuring dedicated capacity throughput and for generating customer-facing acceptance artifacts. Focus on consistent measurement semantics, traffic shaping, and pass/fail criteria that map to committed throughput SLAs.
motivation: Customers purchasing Dedicated capacity require reproducible guarantees for throughput and predictable autoscaling behavior. Existing ad-hoc runs vary by harness, workload, and client settings. We need a single authoritative lab and acceptance criteria used by engineering, SRE, and sales/CS for validation and contracts.
proposed_solution: Create a modular "load lab" harness that: (1) runs canonical traffic profiles against a target fleet topology, (2) reports unified metrics and traces, (3) produces an acceptance report and artifact set for customers, and (4) integrates with CI for automated regression checks. The harness will support both synthetic token-level workloads and recorded customer prompt replays. We'll provide configuration presets for common SLAs (e.g., 100k tokens/min sustained with 95th latency < 250ms) and a library of validators to assert pass/fail rules.
architecture_notes: The harness is separate from the runtime but uses the same client libraries and instrumentation. Key components: traffic-generator (k6-based shim + python reconstructor), scenario catalog (traffic profiles + sequence length distributions), measurement-collector (Prometheus + custom exporters), and report generator (HTML + json summary). Runs happen in isolated test projects/environments to avoid noisy neighbors.
test_plan: 1) Define canonical traffic profiles for small/medium/large customers. 2) Implement traffic generator adapters for sync and streaming endpoints. 3) Validate metric collection against our runtime telemetry. 4) Execute baseline runs on a standardized fleet topology. 5) Create acceptance report template and checklist. 6) Run customer-acceptance scenario using recorded prompts for two pilot customers.
scenarios: steady-state sustained throughput (T60): run for 60 minutes at target token/sec and observe stability
burst recovery: inject short high-rate bursts and validate autoscaling & latency recovery
ramp-up and ramp-down: progressive load increases to validate autoscale thresholding and cooldown
long-tail latency: track 95th and 99th token latency under sustained load
mixed-characteristics: variable sequence lengths and tokenization patterns to test batching efficiency
traffic_profiles: profile-small: 10k tokens/min, median seq 64, 90% short completions
profile-medium: 60k tokens/min, median seq 128, mixed short/medium
profile-large: 250k tokens/min, median seq 512, 30% long sequences
customer-replay: captured prompt set + user think-times from pilot customer
success_criteria: A run passes if: (1) sustained tokens_per_second >= target +/- 3% for the T60 window, (2) p95_latency_ms <= SLA threshold for profile, (3) error_rate_percent < 0.5% for the run, and (4) no persistent queue growth > 3 minutes. For customer-acceptance artifacts, include reproducible run config, raw metrics, and a signed report from the SRE on duty.
failure_modes: Transient overload leading to increased errors, autoscaler misconfiguration causing oscillation, degraded KV cache hit rate due to sequence distribution mismatch, kernel scheduling hot path regressions causing p99 spikes.
runbooks: - pre-run: snapshot fleet topology, ensure no maintenance windows, allocate isolated VPC. - during run: monitor top metrics dashboard and abort on >1% error sustained for 5 minutes. - post-run: run artifact collector, archive Prometheus time series and traces, and run diff against baseline.
automation: Add CI job 'dedicated-throughput-gate' that runs a smoke T5 profile on merge for runtime changes. Add nightly scheduled full-profile runs against a canary fleet and upload artifacts to the artifacts bucket.
customer_acceptance_process: For contract validation: run full-profile in a customer-allocated environment or use anonymized replay; produce signed acceptance report with config, metrics, and recommendations. Offer remediation steps if run fails: adjust autoscaler policy, recommend model quantization, or change batching config. CS and SRE to jointly sign off.
communication_plan: Share initial lab spec with PM and SRE for feedback (week 0). Run pilot with 2 customers (week 2). Publish 'how we measure throughput' doc and acceptance report template in Confluence (week 3). Sync with Sales/Legal to align contract language (week 4).
risks: - Overfitting harness to our test topology (mitigation: include variability in topology). - Customer environments vary; acceptance runs may need environment-specific baselines. - Instrumentation gaps that cause mismatched metrics between lab and production.
next_steps: 1) Merge baseline harness PR and ship a first-run artifact. 2) Run pilot acceptance with two committed customers. 3) Iterate pass/fail thresholds based on pilot feedback and SRE review.
notes: Keep the harness lightweight so it can run in both hosted and dedicated testing zones. Avoid hard-coded secrets in artifacts. Use canonical model checkpoints defined in the model catalog for reproducibility.
